title: Initially recorded plant taxa kept an abundance-ratio gap at warm sites in 20 transplant gradients
abstract: We tested whether changes only in initially unrecorded taxa can remove the final plant composition gap to warm-site controls. We derived a sharp L1 bound that permits arbitrary changes outside a fixed taxon set and compositional dilution, while holding final abundance ratios inside the set fixed. In 40 TransPlant contrasts from 20 gradients, the minimum residual averaged 55.0% of the recorded gap (95% gradient bootstrap limits 44.6-65.8%). A control split also gave a large raw bound. An added equal-sample comparison therefore used the same initial set and target for warmed and control plots. The excess minimum residual was 0.225 L1 units (0.146-0.313). This result requires more than changes outside the initial set under the tested restriction. It does not identify a causal dispersal share: arrivals can alter residents, and soil history, reference choice and recording error remain possible causes. The first census was after treatment. Small samples and an exploratory calibration limit inference. The package includes code, a proof, 1000 independent linear-program checks, aggregate evidence and external-source retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Minimum residual when final abundance ratios among initially recorded taxa stay fixed. Controls show that a raw bound can be large without a treatment difference. Equal-sample paired calibration retains a positive excess in warmed plots. Intervals resample gradients.
